chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Yahya al-Azraq, from Hammad ibn Bashir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Indeed, Allah, Blessed and Exalted, is Kind (Rafiq) and He loves kindness. From His kindness to His servants is that He eases their grudges and their resistance against their desires and their hearts. And from His kindness to them is that He leaves them upon a command, intending to remove them from it as a kindness to them, so that He does not cast upon them the bonds of faith and its burden all at once, causing them to weaken. So when He wills that, He abrogates the command with another, and it becomes abrogated.

key_terms.أَضْغَانَهُمْ: Their grudges, enmities, or strong dislikes
key_terms.تَسْلِيلُهُ: He eases, unties, or makes easy
key_terms.رَفِيقٌ: Kind, Gentle, One who is gentle with His servants

ai.seo_question: How does God's kindness manifest in the gradual imposition of religious duties?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi elucidates the divine attribute of Rafiq (Gentleness) by illustrating how God employs gradualism (tadrij) in legislation to accommodate human capacity. By easing initial burdens and abrogating commands progressively, He prevents the overwhelming of the soul, ensuring the firm establishment of faith's bonds without causing spiritual collapse.
